rules.statement: Implement a filtered read as a discrete, intent-named store method that pushes the filter to the database, never by paging or listing the whole set and filtering the materialized items in memory.
rules.why: Fetch-all-then-filter uses no index, transfers every row and child collection only to discard most, and the waste compounds when several readers in one request re-scan the same set.
rules.check: Look for a service calling GetPageAsync or another list read on a store and then applying Where/filtering on the results in memory; it should call a dedicated store method instead.

rules.statement: Don't expose IQueryable or Expression parameters on a store interface; name the method for what it fetches and let each backend translate it.
rules.why: Expression parameters tie the contract to an ORM, let the caller shape the SQL, and force a non-EF backend to interpret expression trees.
rules.check: Look for store interface methods taking or returning IQueryable<T> or Expression<Func<...>>.

rules.statement: Give a store reader that needs only a few columns a lightweight projection type so the query never joins or materializes unneeded child collections; load the full entity only when the reader needs it.
rules.why: Materializing child collections such as settings or secrets for a reader that uses a few columns wastes transfer and work.
rules.check: Look for new store reads that return full entities with Include of child collections when the caller only uses a few scalar fields.

rules.statement: Use a store's GetPageAsync only for genuine unfiltered pagination such as management lists, not as a filtering mechanism.
rules.why: Pagination over the whole set is not a substitute for a pushed-down filter.
rules.check: Look for GetPageAsync calls whose results are filtered, searched, or looped to completion to find a subset.

rules.statement: When a case-sensitive value is filtered through a case-folded normalized column, treat the database filter as a widening pre-filter and re-apply the exact case-sensitive match in memory over the returned set; keep exact predicates such as booleans and id-set membership wholly in the database.
rules.why: The normalized column provides uniqueness and sargability and never drops a true match, but values like scopes and resource identifiers compare case-sensitively under RFC 6749 and RFC 8707.
rules.check: Look for queries on Normalized* columns whose results are used without an exact ordinal comparison, or for exact predicates evaluated in memory instead of in the query.

rules.statement: Don't place a cache or invalidation seam under store read methods or make correctness depend on cache freshness; layer any cache on top without changing the store contract.
rules.why: Correctness must not depend on cache freshness, and a cache can be added later on top if profiling demands it.
rules.check: Look for store interfaces or implementations gaining cache/invalidation parameters or methods, or per-request caches of full reads used to avoid adding a filtered method.

rules.statement: Pass an optional, growing set of selection criteria as a readonly record struct with init-only, non-required properties built with object initializers or `with`, never as positional or optional method parameters or a positional constructor.
rules.why: A store interface is implemented by consumers, so a new positional parameter changes the signature and breaks source and binary compatibility for every implementer and caller.
rules.check: Look for store or service methods gaining another optional filter parameter, or criteria types with positional constructors or required members.

rules.statement: Keep a required identity key that is the operation's subject as a positional parameter rather than wrapping it in a criteria DTO.
rules.why: A required key is not a growing filter and gains nothing from an optional bag of properties; the rule is optional-and-growing is a DTO, required key is positional.
rules.check: Look for required ids moved into optional criteria DTO properties, or DTOs wrapping a single required key.

rules.statement: Give a criteria DTO an IsEmpty guard when an empty filter would act on everything, such as a bulk revoke or delete, and check it before acting.
rules.why: An empty filter on a bulk operation would affect every record.
rules.check: Look for bulk update/delete/revoke methods taking a criteria DTO without an IsEmpty check guarding the unscoped case.

rules.statement: Take pagination as a single page-request object (cursor plus required limit) rather than separate positional cursor and limit parameters.
rules.why: A positional (cursor, limit) pair cannot gain a sort direction without a signature change.
rules.check: Look for paged methods with separate cursor and limit parameters.

rules.statement: Model request and command inputs as init-only records rather than types with positional constructors.
rules.why: They grow like criteria, and init-only properties let them gain members without breaking callers.
rules.check: Look for new *Request or *Command types declared as positional records or with constructor-only initialization.
